reference.comment: Same first-party HF Transformers integration as the Apache-2.0 sibling, on the same code path: granite_speech5_ctc / granite_speech5_encoder, GraniteSpeech5ForCTC, GraniteSpeech5FeatureExtractor and GraniteSpeech5Processor from mainline transformers >= 5.16 (dumped with 5.17.0). No trust_remote_code - config.json has no auto_map. config.json, preprocessor_config.json, processor_config.json and generation_config.json are BYTE-IDENTICAL to the sibling repo and the 550 shipped tensor names are an exact set match, so the encoder reference is literally the same code on the same shapes; the dumper is reused unmodified (--model is its only repo-dependent input). The dumper mirrors the model card path: AutoProcessor + AutoModelForCTC + model.generate + processor.batch_decode(skip_special_tokens=True). attn_implementation=eager (GraniteSpeech5 sets _supports_flash_attn=False because the Shaw relative-position bias is a float attention mask). The WEIGHTS differ from the sibling's: this variant is trained on ~75,000 h (adds GigaSpeech 10,000 h and SPGI Speech 4,900 h) against the sibling's ~60,000 h, so nothing numerical may be reused across variants. The repo ALSO ships the same stale ctc_conformer remote code (granite_encoder.py, modeling_ctc_conformer.py), byte-identical to the sibling's copies and equally unable to load this checkpoint; it is not the reference.
reference.dump_args_comment: Dump ALL 16 encoder blocks, not the dumper's 6-block default (0,1,2,7,8,15). Added at Stage 4: blocks 10-13 carry a massive-activation channel (570) at |value| 190-481 while the rest of those tensors sit at 20-28, and it dominates this variant's BF16 drift. Without these blocks the drift is only observable after the fact at enc.out and cannot be localized. tests/tolerances/granite5_ctc-nc.json gates all 34 resulting tensors.

oracle_dtype_comment: Weights ship BF16 and transformers' dtype='auto' would load BF16, but the dumps and the reference WER baseline are both taken at F32, matching the Apache-2.0 sibling's oracle so the two variants stay comparable. The BF16->F32 upcast is lossless, so these are the shipped weights unchanged, and F32 activations over BF16 weights is exactly the transcribe.cpp compute regime. The sibling measured a BF16 forward as transcript- and token-identical but up to 2-3% of p99_abs away from F32 (~250x the 1e-4 x p99_abs Stage 2 budget); the architecture is identical here, so a BF16 oracle would force the same blind tolerance widening at Stage 4.

frontend.comment: GraniteSpeech5FeatureExtractor. torchaudio.transforms.MelSpectrogram(sr=16000, n_fft=512, win_length=400, hop_length=160, n_mels=80) at library defaults: power=2.0, Hann PERIODIC, center=True, pad_mode=reflect, f_min=0, f_max=8000, mel_scale=htk, norm=None (UNNORMALIZED triangular filters, not Slaney). win_length=400 != n_fft=512, so the window is zero-padded to 512 inside the STFT. Then clamp_min(1e-10) -> log10 -> per-utterance floor at (global max over BOTH time and mel bins) - 8.0 -> fixed affine x/4 + 1. That normalization is bit-for-bit src/transcribe-mel.cpp's existing per_utterance mode ((x+4)/4); it is a dynamic-range floor, NOT CMVN. Then concat torchaudio.functional.compute_deltas(win_length=3) along the channel axis (80 -> 160) and stack 2 consecutive frames (160 -> 320). FRAMING: mel_frames = n_samples // 160; num_frames = 2*ceil(mel_frames/2); the WAVEFORM is right-padded to (num_frames-1)*160+1 samples; the melspec is sliced to [..., :num_frames]. For even mel_frames this drops one trailing center-pad frame; for odd mel_frames it keeps it. The trailing partial stacking group is VALID, not masked: encoder_frame_counts = ceil(mel_frames/2) equals the emitted frame count (verified valid=550/550 on jfk, 1767/1767 on dots).

tokenizer_summary.comment: SentencePiece-derived BPE, NOT the byte-level BPE of the Apache-2.0 sibling. This is the only structural difference between the two variants. 30161 merges, byte_fallback=true, unk_token=<unk>. Normalizer Sequence[Replace(CRLF -> LFLF), Precompiled(charsmap)] is ENCODE-side only and inert for CTC inference. pre_tokenizer null. Decoder Sequence[Replace(U+2581 -> ' '), ByteFallback, Fuse, Strip(' ', start=1)]. Vocabulary layout: id 0 = <unk>, simultaneously the CTC blank and pad_token_id (the PIECE differs from the sibling's <|blank|>; the ID is 0 on both); ids 1..254 = 254 reserved placeholders <|tok0|>..<|tok253|> with no training signal, declared special=false and reachable by greedy argmax with no suppression in the reference; ids 255..510 = the 256 byte-fallback pieces <0x00>..<0xFF>; ids 511..16383 = SentencePiece word pieces, 12918 of which carry a leading U+2581. The model id space is 1:1 with the tokenizer - no offset, no special-token block to strip. tokenizer_config.json declares tokenizer_class=ParakeetTokenizer, which is load-bearing on both variants: ParakeetTokenizer._decode is where the CTC run-length collapse lives. GGUF must emit tokenizer.ggml.model="bpe" (-> DecodeMode::SentencePiece); emitting "gpt2" would produce mojibake on every U+2581, and tokenizer.ggml.pre="granite" is meaningless here. The two vocabularies SHARE NO IDS ('the' is 406 on the sibling, 515 here) and config.json is byte-identical between the repos, so a crossed checkpoint/tokenizer pairing loads cleanly and emits fluent-looking garbage - vocab_sha256 is the only guard. vocab_sha256: 3735804bd7e9167ed5c02aafb832e9253bb586618bd7d51d85dc5a5ad9076f91 (sibling: 3a2c2ef57ee23c9ecbe72f220b9c1e838783df49a159082c39f9ed91c32e7fde).

capabilities.comment: Monolingual English encoder-CTC with no timestamp surface, identical to the Apache-2.0 sibling. CTC emission frames do not provide trustworthy word durations and upstream publishes no alignment reference, so segment, word and token timestamp requests are unsupported. Upstream publishes benchmarks only as bar-chart images; the single numeric public figure for this variant is 4.85% aggregate Open ASR leaderboard WER (the sibling scores 5.00%), with a stated advantage on SPGI Speech and a disadvantage on the chunked Earnings22 set - so that ordering is not a prediction for test-clean. Stage 4 and Stage 7 gate against THIS variant's measured Oracle reference baseline on LibriSpeech test-clean (reports/wer/granite-speech-5.0-470m-turboctc-nc-REF.test-clean.{jsonl,score.json}), never against the sibling's measured numbers.

tolerance_file_comment: Per-variant, deliberately NOT tests/tolerances/granite5_ctc.json. That file is flat per-tensor and is Stage-4-finalized for the Apache-2.0 sibling; the two variants have different weights and will drift differently, so they cannot share a budget. Precedent: whisper-base.json, qwen3_asr-1.7b.json.
cases_comment: Same two cases as the Apache-2.0 sibling, for the same reason: jfk has mel_frames=1100 (even) and dots has mel_frames=3533 (odd), which are different code paths in the feature extractor - the odd case right-pads the waveform and keeps the trailing center-pad frame, the even case drops it. dots (35.3 s) also spans many more 128-frame attention blocks than jfk (11.0 s). The feature extractor is byte-identical across variants, so this coverage requirement is unchanged.
